name: Sign-Autocorrelation z Score
note: Estimates whether the SIGN of a bar return persists at lag m, and trades only when that persistence is statistically significant. p_m is the continuation frequency over the last N valid sign pairs (bars with a zero return are dropped from the pairing rather than counted as up), and z_m = (2*p_m - 1)*sqrt(N) against the random-walk null of 0.5. z <= -threshold takes the OPPOSITE side to the last bar's sign, z >= +threshold takes the SAME side, and nothing is taken in between. Magnitude is deliberately absent from the statistic and appears only as an entry filter, |r_t| >= r_min * stdev(r, r_win). The hold is exactly m bars, implemented in exit_signal from the position's own entry bar so that sweeping the lag sweeps the hold with it, which a fixed time_stop could not do.
source: arXiv 2606.29591, 'The Bounce Has No Direction' -- the FRI sign test, rho_sign(m) = 2*p_{m,0} - 1 with p_{m,0} the continuation frequency and 0.5 the random-walk null; the paper reports z_sign = -1.59 at lag 1 (insignificant) alongside rho(1) = -0.081 with z* = -7.39, and z_sign = -2.32 at lag 3 where rho(3) is insignificant.
